apps.name: rsh
apps.summary: Ruby that also runs command lines: one script for the logic and the commands
apps.description:
rsh is a script interpreter: Ruby with a shell layer. Write the logic in Ruby and the commands as command lines, in one file that starts with #!/usr/bin/rsh.

Pipes, redirections, jobs, traps and globbing work as in a shell; strings, arrays, hashes and blocks work as in Ruby. One program with its interpreter built in, under 3 MB, with a man page (man rsh).
apps.author: wonderlandos

plugins.name: Battery Care
plugins.summary: Battery health and charge cycles, and a reminder to unplug at the charge you choose.
plugins.description:
Battery Care tells you how worn your laptop's battery is and helps it last longer.

The desktop card shows the battery's health: how much it holds now compared with when it was new, in watt-hours, and how many charge cycles it has been through.

The menu bar item reminds you to unplug the charger once the battery reaches the charge you choose (80% unless you change it), with one notification per charge. Click it to change the charge, turn the reminder off, or see the details.

On a computer without a battery it says so and does nothing else.

plugins.name: Load Graph
plugins.summary: CPU and memory over the last minutes as small graphs, on a desktop card and in the menu bar.
plugins.description:
Load Graph answers the question a single number cannot: has the computer been busy for a while, or was that just a spike?

The desktop card draws CPU and memory use over the last six minutes, with the highest point and the load average. The menu bar item draws the last half minute of CPU next to the figure now. Click it to open Top.

The figures come from the same system report the Stats plugin uses. Nothing is saved: the graphs start again when you log in.

plugins.name: Net Speed
plugins.summary: Download and upload speed in the menu bar, and a card with the last two minutes.
plugins.description:
Net Speed shows how fast this computer is downloading and uploading right now.

The menu bar item shows both speeds and refreshes every two seconds; click it for each network connection and how much it has moved since the computer started. The desktop card draws the last two minutes as a small graph.

It counts every real connection (Wi-Fi, Ethernet, VPN) and leaves out the computer's own loopback and the virtual bridges containers and virtual machines make. It reads the counters the system already keeps; it sends nothing anywhere.

plugins.name: Quiet Hours
plugins.summary: Do Not Disturb on a schedule: on every evening at the hour you choose, off in the morning.
plugins.description:
Quiet Hours turns on Do Not Disturb at the hour you choose and turns it off again when the quiet time ends: from 22:00 to 07:00 unless you change it. Notifications wait in Notification Center instead of popping up, and urgent ones still show.

Click the moon in the menu bar to change the hours or pause the schedule. If you turn Do Not Disturb off yourself during quiet time, Quiet Hours leaves it off until the next quiet time; it only ever turns off what it turned on.

The first time it turns Do Not Disturb on, WolOS asks whether Quiet Hours may do that. Choose Always Allow so it works when you are not at the computer; you can take that back in Settings, Assistants & Automation.

plugins.name: Web Shortcuts
plugins.summary: Search Wikipedia, the Arch Wiki, GitHub and nine more sites from the menu bar, in two clicks.
plugins.description:
Web Shortcuts searches a website without opening the browser first. Click the magnifier in the menu bar, type what you are looking for, and press Search next to the site: Wikipedia, Wiktionary, the Arch Wiki, Arch packages, GitHub, MDN Web Docs, Rust crates, Stack Overflow, YouTube, OpenStreetMap, DuckDuckGo or the manual pages. The site's own search opens in your browser.

With nothing typed, the button opens the site itself. The words stay in the box until you change them, so you can try the same search on several sites.

The plugin only builds the address; your browser opens it. Nothing is read from the web, and what you type is not saved.
